international.title: UK will miss climate targets if it weakens EV sales rules, advisers warn
international.summary: Analysts say mooted move to let more petrol and diesel vehicles be sold would wreck plan to reach net zero by 2050 Weakening the UK’s electric car sales rules would probably cause the government to miss legally binding climate targets, according to advisers tracking Britain’s progress to net zero. The analysis by the Climate Change Committee (CCC) suggests the policy would blow a hole in the plan for achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050 – prompting concerns that Andy Burnham’s government will have to slash the UK’s carbon emissions reduction targets, known as the carbon budgets.
